reviews.body: Thanks. I checked it on top of main: the backend unit tests pass, and the direct Anthropic requests are unchanged from #1979 (Sonnet 5.5 uses output_config, Opus 5 and Haiku 4.5 still force the tool).

comments.body:
Thanks for picking up the Bedrock and Vertex part. One case I ran into while looking at the same adapters, in case it's useful:

`_avoid_forced_tool_choice` only registers `supports_output_config` when the model is missing from `litellm.model_cost`:

```python
if name not in litellm.model_cost and f"{self._litellm_provider_id}/{name}" not in litellm.model_cost:
    litellm.register_model(...)
```

So if LiteLLM already lists the model without that capability, nothing is registered. That can happen with LiteLLM's remote model map, which LiteLLM fetches at import unless `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True` is set. With 1.100.4, the remote map I got (7,099 entries, versus 3,410 bundled) lists `us.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5` as a `bedrock_converse` entry with `supports_native_structured_output: False`. A test module, or an application, that imports `litellm` before `beeai_framework` therefore gets the remote map. In that case `output_config` may be dropped again and the forced `json_tool_call` returns. The unit tests wouldn't notice, because offline runs use the bundled map.

Two small changes would cover it:
- register when the entry lacks the capability, not only when it is missing, by merging the flag into the existing entry so its pricing fields are kept: `litellm.register_model({key: {**litellm.model_cost[key], "supports_output_config": True}})`;
- pin `litellm.model_cost` to a copy of the bundled map in the new tests (`GetModelCostMap.load_local_model_cost_map()`), and add one case that pre-seeds an affected id without the capability.

I haven't run this branch, so please treat it as something to check rather than a confirmed failure. The same "skip if listed" guard was already in the Anthropic adapter from #1979.

Thanks @leninworld, both points are addressed in 8ac14a36 (pushed on top, no force):

- When LiteLLM already lists the model but without the `output_config` capability, the flag is now merged into the existing entry instead of being skipped, so its pricing and other fields are kept.
- New test that starts from the bundled model map and checks the merged entry.

The earlier Bedrock/Vertex tests were not changed and still pass with the merge (test_litellm_chat.py: 103 passed).

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
